item.title: Green Flag Red Flag - Domestic Violence Awareness — Tue Sep 22, 7:00 PM — Freeman Hall
item.description:
Relationships can be exciting, complicated, and sometimes hard to navigate, but you don’t have to do it alone. Join us to learn how to recognize red and green flags in relationships and build stronger boundaries. We’ll discuss dating trends, common dating misconceptions, and ways to build healthier relationships while connecting you with resources and support available both on and off campus. Leave with a better sense of what you want and deserve in a relationship, along with the tools to help you get there. All are welcome! September 22nd Freeman Hall 7PM-9PM

item.title: Food Tour of South Orange — Sat Sep 26, 11:00 AM
item.description: Hosted by Chow Town Food Tour What do Lauryn Hill, Paul Auster and Zach Braff have in common? They’re all from South Orange, NJ! Over the last century, this formerly sleepy farm town has bloomed into a thriving satellite community of Newark and NYC. Tour guests will enjoy this 3-hour walking tour of the vibrant village of South Orange and taste what makes this an unsung gem of NJ’s food scene. Chow Town’s classic tour, built for fun & flavors. Distance: about 1/2 mile. item.title: Lego Robotics for Elementary Students — Sat Sep 26, 1:00 PM — RecRoom
item.description: LEGO Robotics for Elementary Kids (Grades K–5) LEGO Robotics at Kinetic Minds introduces kids to engineering and beginner coding through hands-on building, testing, and problem-solving using LEGO robotics kits. In this small-group, drop-in friendly workshop, kids work in pairs to build real robots, program simple behaviors, and improve their designs through guided challenges. The focus is on curiosity, experimentation, and learning how things work—there’s no single “right” build and no step-by-step cookie-cutter instructions. Workshops are intentionally capped at a low student-to-instructor ratio to support collaboration, confidence, and meaningful learning. Kids will explore: • Engineering and building with LEGO robotics components • Beginner coding concepts (motors, sensors, cause and effect) • Testing, debugging, and iterating designs • Teamwork, communication, and explaining ideas Details: • 60-minute session • Small-group format • No prior experience required Community Spons

item.title: Acolyte Training #1 — Sun Sep 27, 11:30 AM
item.description: Is your child sixth grade or older? Would s/he like to be an acolyte? A what? According to The Episcopal Church website, an acolyte is defined as "A general term which covers not only servers, torchbearers, and lighters of candles but also crucifers, thurifers, and banner-bearers."At Holy Spirit Verona, sixth to eighth grade students have a Sunday School class offered twice a month. On the non-class Sundays, sixth to 8th grade students are encouraged to be torchbearers, banner-bearers and second cross bearer at times on weeks when there is no junior/high school Sunday School Class. And on the non-class Sundays, ninth to twelfth grade students can be lead cross bearers at times if interested. Confirmation Students can use this time at "service" or "outreach hours."We will host two training sessions this fall for new acolytes -- attendance at ONE sessions is enough, but if your child wants to attend both that works too! Meet at the Ushers' Table in the Sanctuary at 11:30am on either/both

item.title: Inner Body Meditation (20 minutes) — Thu Oct 1, 9:30 PM
item.description:
The Mindful Stream "Awareness of the inner body takes you beyond the mind." - Eckhart Tolle
In this mediation session we will bring our attention here: to the inner body. Sessions are suitable for newcomers, those experienced in Tolle's teachings and anyone wishing to remain completely anonymous. They will last around 20 minutes and cameras and microphones will be disabled. (Depending on the situation, a free discussion may be held at the end with mics and cameras allowed.)
See you there!
Please be aware that sessions will close if no members have joined after 10 minutes.
Emrys also organises a free Work of Byron Katie online mediation group. Visit [this Meetup Group link](https://www.meetup.com/thework-runsfree/) for more information.21

item.description: Is your child sixth grade or older? Would s/he like to be an acolyte? A what? On the non-class Sundays, sixth to 8th grade students are encouraged to be torchbearers, banner-bearers and second cross bearer at times on weeks when there is no junior/high school Sunday School Class. item.title: What Does Brotherhood Mean to You? — Mon Oct 12, 8:30 PM — University Hall 3048 - Classroom
item.description:
An interactive conversation exploring the meaning of brotherhood beyond simply being part of a fraternity or organization. The event will open with students writing their personal definition of brotherhood on a shared board or wall. Those responses will then serve as conversation starters for a facilitated discussion about what brotherhood looks like in everyday life. The discussion can explore topics such as trust, accountability, vulnerability, support, loyalty, healthy masculinity, friendship, and showing up for one another during difficult times. Facilitators can introduce different scenarios and questions that encourage participants to think about the difference between saying someone is your brother and actually demonstrating brotherhood through your actions.
Hosted by: Lambda Sigma Upsilon Latino Fraternity, Inc.

item.title: Spiritual Enrichment Group: Check-In — Mon Oct 19, 7:00 PM
item.description:
Our Spiritual Enrichment Group is now meeting on the third Monday of the month at 7pm via Zoom. For many years we met at 11:45am (originally in-person and since the pandemic) via Zoom. In Spring 2026, Reverend Katherine sent the following message to our Church lay leaders: "Coffee hour is growing and newcomers are still walking through our doors. It is the only time that clergy has an opportunity to interact and be available to the congregation. Hanging around during clean up is a further opportunity as well. Exiting into an office with a closed door does not seem appropriate anymore."And so, members of the Spiritual Enrichment Group agreed to try meeting on Monday evenings; we use the Sunday Morning Worship Zoom Link. In certain seasons, we'll host a more regular (weekly) gathering using an agreed upon program. If you have any questions, speak with Reverend Katherine.
Source: Church of the Holy Spirit Verona

item.title: What is a Man? — Mon Oct 19, 8:30 PM — University Hall 3048 - Classroom
item.description:
What is a Man? is a real and open dialogue centered on the stigmatization of men and the expectations placed on masculinity. This space explores how societal pressures often force men to suppress emotion, struggle in silence, and avoid vulnerability. Through honest conversation, we aim to break down those barriers and address men’s mental health in a meaningful way. It’s a judgment-free environment that encourages reflection, healing, and connection, reminding everyone that redefining strength starts with being able to speak, feel, and be heard.
Hosted by: Lambda Sigma Upsilon Latino Fraternity, Inc.
Additional Information can be found at: https://montclair.campuslabs.com/engage/event/12792978
